content:
Should deriving instance for log a warning when we can already synthesize an instance of the shape being derived for the given type? (I'm imagining that such a warning would be silenceable by a set_option.)

The use case I'm imagining is: an upstream type does not have some instance, so I include deriving instance downstream. Then upstream eventually does provide an instance, and now my downstream deriving introduces another instance without me knowing.

Sorry, I have no idea how this ended up in #new members; I thought I was posting in #lean4. :upside_down: (If anyone would like to move the above message, that'd be welcome; I'd delete and repost, but I don't think I'm allowed to delete topics.)

EDIT: Oh, I know how this happened: I was scrolling through search results for "deriving instance" and must have started to compose a message when a #new members post was scrolling by. Then when I clicked on #lean4, it kept me in #new members. Obviously this is my fault, but I'm still kind of surprised I can start to send a message to a topic from search results without clicking on any search result... :eyes:
